title: How does a radio pick ONE station?

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: How does my radio pick one station?
short_scenes.narration: Hundreds of stations fill the air. How does Volt's radio pick just one?
At one frequency, the inductor and capacitor cancel, and the current peaks. That's resonance.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: An inductor blocks high frequencies, a capacitor blocks low ones. At one frequency they cancel each other perfectly, and only that station gets through strongly.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Turning the knob changes C, which moves the peak onto your station.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: For the detailed explanation, watch the full video on our channel. It's part of our complete Network Theory course.
